newsitem.title: UK: German cocoa grind data under scrutiny by ICCO.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa grind data under scrutiny by ICCO.

text.p: Cocoa analysts reviewing stocks estimates of the International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) concluded that German figures may need an upward revision, trade sources said on Friday.

A working group consisting of ICCO delegates, analysts and senior members of trade on Thursday looked at the possibility of under-reporting in German grinds which the ICCO uses to calculate changes in stock levels.

There have been reports that a combination of factors such as the introduction of the single European market and reluctance by one or more local processors to disclose data could have led to inaccuracies in grinds.

In the four years from 1991/92 to 1994/95 a discrepancy of some 130,000 tonnes emerged between the stock estimates of the ICCO and the UK-based trade and research group E.D.&F. Man which uses German bean imports instead of grinds.

Hagen Streichert of the German Ministry of Agriculture who leads the German delegation accepted remarks that recent figures could be flawed due to a number of factors including the move to a single market which he said may have complicated reports by trade.
He undertook an overhaul of domestic reporting sources to try to correct any possible errors.
Analysts said however that while this was being carried out, they did not expect the ICCO to shift to using bean imports instead of grinds, which they said forms the correct base for working stocks.
The ICCO uses two weeks of annual grindings to calculate manufacturers' working stocks in Western Europe.
"I think they'll stick to using grind figures if they can. Otherwise you're washing your hands of the problem," said Fish who is the managing director of UK-based cocoa reseach group PCR Ltd.
The working group has also concluded that the ICCO's estimate for world stocks of 1.4 million tonnes for end-September 1996 was too high and should be revised down.
